title: Leadership in Times of Change: How to Turn Uncertainty into Personal and Professional Growth
summary: Discover how leadership, self-leadership, and talent management help address uncertainty, drive growth, and strengthen teams.
body_markdown:
## How to Stay Focused on Your Purpose When Everything Changes


### Why Is Leadership More Important Than Ever in Times of Uncertainty?


Leadership becomes especially relevant when technological, economic, and organizational changes create uncertainty about the future. At such times, people need guidance, direction, and opportunities to continue growing professionally.


Companies are undergoing constant transformation. Artificial intelligence automates tasks and redefines professions; geopolitical tensions disrupt markets and supply chains; regulation, competition, and new customer expectations force decisions to be made at an unprecedented pace.


In this scenario, the greatest risk isn’t just falling behind technologically. It’s that people will no longer see themselves reflected in the work they do. Some professionals keep their jobs but lose projects, responsibilities, or opportunities through which they could add value. When the challenge disappears, the emotional bond with the organization can also weaken.


## What is self-leadership, and how does it help people cope with professional changes?


Self-leadership is the ability to take responsibility for one’s own development, especially when circumstances change or professional difficulties arise.


Losing an important responsibility can feel like a loss of professional identity. The way forward begins with self-leadership: acknowledging the disappointment without getting stuck in it, separating personal worth from the position held, and regaining control over what still depends on oneself.


Psychology refers to the ability to accept difficult emotions without letting them dictate our behavior as “psychological flexibility.” In the workplace, this attitude can be complemented by “job crafting”: seeking out new challenges, relationships, and learning opportunities to rebuild a space from which to contribute once again.


Self-leadership does not mean denying an uncomfortable situation or justifying any decision. It means not letting that situation have the final say over our career path. When the responsibility we receive from outside decreases, the responsibility we take on for ourselves must increase—at least temporarily. No one can guarantee us the next opportunity, but we can prepare ourselves so that it finds us learning, contributing, and still moving forward.


## Benefits of Self-Leadership


- Greater adaptability.
- Better emotional management.
- Continuous skill development.
- Ability to identify new opportunities.
- Increased professional resilience.
- Greater autonomy in career management.


## How Should a Leader Communicate Difficult Changes?


Communication is one of the most important responsibilities of leadership. Even necessary decisions can have negative effects when they are not explained properly.


Business changes require difficult decisions. Not all of them will be popular, nor will all of them be right the first time. However, even a necessary decision can cause avoidable harm when communicated in a hurry, coldly, or out of frustration.


The answer begins with the leader’s emotional self-regulation: acknowledging fear, fatigue, or the need for control before those emotions dictate the tone of the conversation. Next comes fairness in approach: consistent standards, respectful treatment, and honest explanations.


Effective communication requires answering four questions: what is changing, why is it changing, how does it affect people, and what possibilities does it open up? It also requires admitting what is not yet known and truly listening. When communication has created distance, trust is not restored by sending more messages, but through presence, consistency, and the willingness to correct mistakes.


Apologizing for inappropriate behavior does not undermine authority; it demonstrates maturity. A leadership position may be granted through an appointment, but its legitimacy is renewed in every conversation. People may forget some details of the change, but they are unlikely to forget how they were treated during times of uncertainty.


## What characterizes leadership that fosters talent?


One of the key indicators of leadership is the ability to develop others’ potential and amplify talent within an organization.


Periods of transformation reveal the true quality of leadership. Under pressure, some leaders close ranks around the teams they already know. That reaction may offer an immediate sense of control, but it also creates silos, limits learning, and excludes capabilities that the organization needs.


A team is not private property—it is a temporary responsibility. Leading means intelligently distributing challenges, opening up opportunities, and helping each person discover how far they can go. The best leader does not create dependency; they develop professionals capable of doing certain things better than they can.


A friend who is an entrepreneur once told me that one of his most important decisions had been to surround himself with good people whose talents surpassed his own. That is one of the great truths of leadership: those who feel they must always be the brightest person in the room end up overshadowing everyone else. The true leader does not fear the talent of others; they identify it, connect it, and provide space for it to grow.


## Benefits of Developing Talent


- More autonomous teams.
- Greater innovation.
- Better collaboration.
- Increased collective learning.
- Greater adaptability.
- Sustainable organizational development.


## How Can Leadership Turn Business Transformation into Growth for People?


Business transformation is sustainable when it combines innovation, competitiveness, and talent development.


The new vision defines “Telefónica as the best gateway for citizens to digital technologies” and envisions a more innovative and competitive company, capable of offering more and better services to customers through ambitious, rigorous, and effective management. It also places talent development, the recruitment and retention of highly qualified professionals, and building customer trust among its top priorities.


That value proposition does not begin with technology. It begins with the people who envision it, build it, operate it, and turn it into real solutions.


Transforming and growing cannot mean merely simplifying processes, incorporating artificial intelligence, or gaining efficiency. It must also mean expanding capabilities, connecting knowledge, and offering opportunities for talent to continue evolving.


We won’t be able to offer more and better services if we internally reduce the spaces where the best ideas are born. We won’t be able to build trust in the market if we allow mistrust to grow within the organization. And we’ll hardly be able to help our clients break down their digital barriers if we aren’t capable of first breaking down the ones that separate our own teams.


Ultimately, the true measure of a transformation lies not only in the technology adopted or the speed of change. It lies in the doors we are able to open and, above all, in the people we choose not to leave out.


## What is the purpose of leadership in transformation processes?


Leadership enables us to:


- Manage uncertainty constructively.
- Maintain team engagement.
- Facilitate adaptation to change.
- Develop talent.
- Build trust.
- Improve communication.
- Connect technological transformation with people.
- Create opportunities for professional growth.


## Frequently Asked Questions About Leadership and Transformation


**What is self-leadership?**


It is the ability to take responsibility for one’s own development, one’s own decisions, and one’s own adaptation to professional and personal changes.


**Why is psychological flexibility important?**


Because it helps manage difficult emotions without allowing them to dictate all future decisions or actions.


**How should a leader communicate a difficult decision?**


By explaining what is changing, why it is changing, how it affects people, and what opportunities may arise from that change.


**What is one of a leader’s main responsibilities?**


To help people develop their potential and create opportunities for them to continue growing.


**What distinguishes a good leader from a bad leader?**


The ability to develop talent, build trust, and turn changes into opportunities for learning and growth.


**What role do people play in digital transformation?**


People are the ones who design, implement, operate, and turn technology into real solutions for customers and organizations
